entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please wait while we connect you to the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?
I can certainly look into that for you. Could I start with your name and the email address associated with your VeloFit account?
Mark Peterson. The email is m.peterson@email.com.
Thank you, Mark. I'm pulling up your account now... Okay, I see you're one of our VIP members, thank you for your loyalty. I see a recent purchase for the VeloBand Cadence Sensor. Is that the item?
Yes. I want to return it.
I understand. To make sure I'm handling this correctly, what specifically is the issue with the band? Is it a technical fault or a matter of preference?
It's just not working. At all.
I'm very sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a little more? For example, is it that it won't sync with the VeloFit app?
It won't sync, the readings are a joke. I just think the thing is defective. I want my money back for this broken piece of plastic.
I completely understand your frustration. A defective product is absolutely not the experience we want for our VeloFit members. Let me just pull up our return policy for you... one moment, please.

Okay, thank you for your patience, Mark. I've reviewed your order, and it looks like it was delivered about two weeks ago. Our policy allows for returns on items within 10 days of delivery, so you are unfortunately outside that timeframe.
Fine. So you'll take it back?

Absolutely. I've just initiated that return for you. I'm sending a pre-paid shipping label to your email on file now. And because you're a VIP member who received a faulty item, I've also gone ahead and added a $25 credit to your account for your next purchase as an apology.
Oh. Well, thank you. That's actually very helpful. I appreciate that.
You are most welcome. We value your business. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
Alright. Well, thank you for calling VeloFit. Have a wonderful day, Mark.
